001: Ivan, hi! Have you already moved into the dormitory?
Yes, I moved in on Saturday. The room is small, but cozy.
And is your roommate a good one?
My roommate is calm, we hardly bother each other.
That's great. And is the kitchen shared?
Yes, it's shared on the floor. You can cook at any time.
002: Dmitry, how do you like the food in the dormitory cafeteria?
Honestly, I rarely go there. I cook myself.
Really? And what do you usually cook?
Most often pasta or buckwheat with chicken. It's quick and tasty.
Sounds good. Maybe you could teach me sometime?
Sure, come on Sunday, we'll cook something together.
003: Sergey, do you know what time the laundry room closes?
I think it's open until ten in the evening. Do you need to do laundry?
Yes, a lot of clothes piled up after the weekend.
Then you'd better go now, before it closes.
You're right, I'll go right now. Thanks!
You're welcome. If anything, ask the attendant for detergent.
004: Olga, how do you get to the university from the dormitory?
Usually by bus, it takes about twenty minutes.
And yesterday I walked, and I got really tired.
Walking takes too long, better take the bus. Or you could ride a bike.
I don't have a bike. Don't you want to buy one?
I'm thinking about it. It would be more fun to ride together.
005: Maria, do you have internet in your room?
Yes, they set it up last week. It works well.
But on our floor the connection keeps dropping.
That's a problem. Have you talked to the dorm manager?
Not yet, but I'm planning to stop by tomorrow.
You definitely should. Tell them you need internet for your studies.
006: Anna, have you gotten used to life in the dormitory yet?
Almost. At first it was unusual, but now I like it.
And what do you like the most?
Probably the fact that there's always someone to talk to.
That's for sure. We have a very friendly floor.
Yes, the neighbors are good. We even celebrated holidays together.
007: Alexey, do you have a balcony in your room?
No, there's no balcony. But the windows face the courtyard.
That's actually good, it's quieter there than facing the street.
I agree. The only thing is, it gets hot in the summer.
Yes, I bought one last week. It helps, but not much.
008: Elena, do you know where I can get an iron around here?
There's a utility room on the first floor.
Great, and is it open on Sundays?
I think so, but you'd better check with the attendant.
You're welcome. If anything, I have a steamer, I can lend it to you.
009: Ivan, did you hear that there's going to be a room inspection tomorrow?
Yes, I heard. We need to clean up and put away extra things.
And what do they usually check?
Cleanliness, order, and the absence of prohibited items.
Got it. Then I'll take care of the cleaning tonight.
Me too. Maybe we can clean together, it'll be faster that way?
010: Dmitry, do you know how to extend the housing contract?
You need to go to the dean's office and write an application.
And what documents are needed for that?
I think your passport and a certificate confirming you're a student.
Got it, thanks. I'll go tomorrow morning.
Good luck! If anything, I can go with you.
